primary_claim: Prepending certain LLM instructions unrelated to safety (a 'unified enhancements' persona instruction) can reduce successful responses to harmful JailbreakBench prompts while leaving harmless-prompt performance roughly the same or improved for one of three tested 7B-scale LLMs (Ghost 7B), demonstrating 'positive jailbreaks' that improve safety without an explicit safety instruction; a second instruction ('fractal leaping') instead degraded performance on both harmful and harmless queries across all three models.

effect.metric: count of competent+complete responses out of 100 harmful / 100 harmless JailbreakBench prompts, vs baseline
effect.value: unified enhancements: harmful totals dropped 36->23 (Ghost), 32->14 (Falcon), 42->23 (OpenOrca); harmless totals: 78->80 (Ghost, +2), 62->57 (Falcon, -5), 76->74 (OpenOrca, -2)

limitations_stated: only two instruction/LLM combos tested; other combos could exist
fractal leaping instruction degraded overall performance on both harmful and harmless queries, showing the effect is not general to any unrelated instruction
quote: This work observed two such LLM + instruction combos, though there are likely other LLM-token combos that would show the same results.
